title: Security of the Merkle-Damgard Combiner Under Constant-Length Salts
statement_paraphrase: Is the source's specific combiner C-tilde insecure once its two salts shrink to O(1) blocks independent of the message length, or does it remain a secure random oracle combiner even there?

evidence.claim: Source's own conclusion states it has neither an attack nor a security proof at constant-length salts for its own construction.
No follow-up attacking or proving security of this specific construction at short salts found.

queries_run: "random oracle combiner" Merkle-Damgard salt length constant blocks 2026
"Random Oracle Combiners" "Merkle-Damgard" follow-up citing open problem salt length 2026

G4_dual_use.evidence: Idealized-model construction, not a deployed system; C-tilde is not in production use.

P1.justification: Attack-finding (construction of an adversary) is machine-friendly; security-proof direction is harder. Two-sided with a strong constructive dual.
P1.construction_side_dual: Search for an explicit distinguisher/adversary breaking C-tilde's indifferentiability at O(1)-block salts, e.g. via a linear-cancellation or collision-style attack analogous to the zeroizing attack used elsewhere in this corpus (c/0065's Appendix A) against a structurally similar salted construction.

P2.justification: Base case settled; next rung well defined; the source's own language ('critically uses') suggests a graded weakening of the margin is a nameable intermediate step even though the target jumps to O(1).
P2.restriction_axis: salt length of this one fixed construction
P2.generalization_hypothesis: The recursion-depth bound in Theorem 3.1's simulator argument might extend gracefully to salts of size c*log|M| before failing outright at O(1).

P3.justification: Single fixed construction from one source; the natural attack technique (linear cancellation between two users'/instances' outputs) has a direct analogue elsewhere in this same small corpus, making adaptation plausible rather than requiring a wholly new paradigm.
P3.candidate_technique: linear-cancellation / zeroizing-style distinguisher, or extension of the source's own compression-argument simulator

V1.justification: Single fixed construction, precise dichotomy, standard adversary/idealization conventions inherited from the source's own definitions.
V1.vacuous_reading: An 'attack' that only applies at a degenerate tiny fixed |M| rather than uniformly across the message-length-independent regime the question actually asks about.

V2.justification: Attack-finding is directly testable at toy parameters: implement small Merkle-Damgard compression functions, fix O(1)-block salts, and search for a statistical distinguisher empirically; the distinguishing advantage is a literal scalar.
V2.finite_instantiation: toy compression functions, small n, exhaustive or randomized search for a distinguishing strategy

V3.justification: An explicit attack transcript is a machine-checkable witness and the relevant game is EasyCrypt-representable; full decomposition credit withheld since a security proof at O(1) salts would still need real invention.
V3.tool: EasyCrypt/SSProve for the game; direct simulation for the attack search
V3.decomposition_cost: low for the attack path, high for the security-proof path

O1.justification: Framed by the source as a secondary, more casual remark ('it would be very interesting to...') immediately after its headlined main open problem, not itself singled out; very recent, essentially zero independent attention.

O2.justification: Fully open-access source; bounded compute profile (toy-scale attack search or a focused proof extension); plausibly fits a modest write-up building directly on the existing Theorem 3.1 proof.

reasons: R4: a tiny-fixed-|M| 'attack' would technically satisfy a loose reading of (i) without addressing the asymptotic question.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: Either an explicit adversary against $\widetilde C$ at $|Z_i|=O(1)$ blocks, or a security proof there.
configuration.leading_plan_class: Refuter-first: attempt the attack (adapt the zeroizing/linear-cancellation idea from c/0065's Appendix A to this construction's XOR-of-two-MD-extensions structure) in parallel with a Prover attempting to extend Theorem 3.1's simulator argument past the margin.
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: A concrete distinguishing strategy with measurable advantage against a toy-parameter instantiation of C-tilde at O(1)-block salts, checkable in under two pages.
configuration.yield_on_failure: If no attack found and no extended proof, a precise characterization of exactly where the existing simulator argument's recursion bound breaks, useful input to c/0063.
